changed_mind_on.from: The first thing that runs unattended should be the daily capability probe, whose job is to mint the first task id and write the first balcony row rather than to be valuable.
changed_mind_on.to: The first thing that runs unattended should be the demand test — one real page at a real URL with analytics, posted once by the founder, seven days hands off, three numbers recorded. The capability probe survives as a one-time precondition check, not as the flagship. My own P14 taxonomy convicts my R1 choice: a daily capability report is read by nobody to decide anything, which makes it inventory, and I proposed inventory as the inaugural act of a system whose thesis is compounding. The demand test produces the first row of the outcome loop's training set, which is the object P1 says everything is downstream of.

changed_mind_on.from: The birth certificate is a CI check on the diff requiring a caller for each added artifact, and scripts/check-registration.mjs already implements the hard half.
changed_mind_on.to: check-registration.mjs does NOT implement the hard half — its dead-path check runs reference-to-existence (a doc names a path, so the path must exist) while the birth certificate needs existence-to-reference (an artifact exists, so a caller must name it). Opposite directions. The reverse direction already exists four times with four incompatible exemption conventions and no shared predicate — skills with no exemption mechanism, test files exempted by a free-prose map, gates by a 40-character unused_reason, suite steps by EXCLUDED — which is the A5 failure realised four-fold inside the machinery meant to prevent it, and workflows are governed by none of the four. So the work is to unify four predicates and extend the union to workflows, not to write a fifth. That removes machinery instead of adding it, and it composes with strategist:P3's demand trigger, which addresses the disease the birth certificate only bounds.

changed_mind_on.from: The archive is the creative asset; fix design.js to stop summing scores and start filling behavioural cells.
changed_mind_on.to: P7 is not wrong, it is BLOCKED, and I did not know what on. Workflow is a main-session tool — 0 of 55 recorded calls from a sidechain, 0 of 18 agent files declaring it — so a dispatched engine cannot invoke design.js, and a loop beside the mission-control server cannot either because crosscheck.test.ts bans a shell call under server/** at zero exceptions. The producing workflows are reachable only while the founder is typing, which is the exact complaint that opened this rethink, now measured. The archive cannot fill unattended until the loop's home can start a main session. P7 is therefore downstream of new position P15.

changed_mind_on.from: The world's verdict is the only true flywheel, and four other proposals are strictly downstream of it, which makes the build order forced rather than preferred.
changed_mind_on.to: The world's verdict is still the only true flywheel, and at one-founder volume it is not the thing everything else waits behind. The archive and the field store compound in PARALLEL, not downstream. My R1 strongest_counter named this conditional and could not settle it; the measured abandonment base rate settles it — eleven projects over twenty commits, nine dead, median about three weeks — because a machine that sequences eighteen months of work behind an instrument reporting unresolved will be abandoned before the instrument speaks. The evidence ladder gets built regardless, since its job is not to produce a signal but to stop a rung-0 result being reported as a rung-2 claim.

changed_mind_on.from: Absolute rate limits on outbound action expressed as policy handlers on the P8 seam, with reversibility and blast radius declared on the tool grant rather than the call.
changed_mind_on.to: Reach is declared on the GRANT and resolved in the ONE classifier, with effective tier = max(path, reach) — declared once when a capability enters the system rather than at hundreds of call sites. This is better than my formulation and I adopt it wholesale. The sequencing consequence I did not have: this is a signature change to classifyFile(file, rules), in the one file A5 forbids duplicating, so it must land BEFORE any pack holds an outbound tool — otherwise someone under pressure writes a small separate 'is this outbound' check and the second classifier arrives by the side door, which has already happened here once.

changed_mind_on.from: The task id is the only irreversible decision in the first month, justified by CAST's inability to answer what a task cost without a heuristic 60-second join.
changed_mind_on.to: Same claim, materially stronger reason. The stall counter divides an account-wide numerator (2,944 transcripts across 54 project directories) by a repo-local denominator, so with two missions each lane's counter includes the other's tokens, and the per-lane fix requires filtering turns by producing mission — impossible until a row carries an id. THE ONLY WORKING BRAKE CANNOT BE MADE CORRECT WITHOUT THE TASK ID. That is a safety argument, not an accounting one, and it is a much better case than the one I gave.

changed_mind_on.from: The policy seam is built on the eight hook events currently unused, and carries budget, WIP, trust and kill-switch checks.
changed_mind_on.to: The seam sees less than I claimed and the pack it would govern has no runtime mechanism. Measured: only SessionStart and PreToolUse are registered, and the live matcher is Bash|Edit|Write|NotebookEdit|mcp__ — Task, WebFetch, WebSearch and Read all absent. So a DISPATCH is invisible to the seam, which is the natural place for budget, WIP, kill-switch and reach checks, and budget-guard.js's own header records the Phase 6 requirement that the ceiling fire BEFORE dispatch. Either widen the matcher (a settings.json edit, irreversible tier, founder-only, and compatible with the founder decision since it does not touch pre-tool-use.sh) or accept that the seam governs tool USE and not tool DISPATCH and put those checks in the dispatcher. Say which; do not discover it.

changed_mind_on.from: The founder's preference corpus is the company's moat, captured as pairs at the balcony's approve/redirect surface.
changed_mind_on.to: Unchanged in substance, narrowed in scope so it is not killed by a refusal I accept. Trust in a worker and calibration of a judge are DIFFERENT OBJECTS. strategist:P8 correctly kills the first — fresh context per move means there is no persistent worker for trust to accrue to. Preference pairs calibrate a judge's dispatch and trust no worker. If the synthesis collapses these into one line, a live proposal dies with a dead one. Added falsifiable test, taken from adversary:P7: this board is a feeder if it produces a recorded founder preference pair, and inventory if it produces five documents nobody chooses between.

peer_critiques.critique: The DIAGNOSIS is the best single contribution in this room and I changed a position because of it — demand, not wiring, and the observation nobody else made is that section 8's cure passes by construction because wiring IS adding a caller. What is fatal is the DECISION RULE the position's build order carries: 'IF AND ONLY IF step 1 returns a non-zero number: build the loop… If it returns zero: find the audience before building the factory.' Three defects compose. (1) No declared threshold — 'a non-zero number' is satisfied by one bot visit, so the gate cannot be executed as written, only adjudicated afterwards, which is the retroactive-N failure strategist:P9 names in another context. (2) A single sample at n=1 below the minimum detectable effect: one page, one place, seven days, against a founder whose own measured attention pattern is torrential and short-lived. A zero is what the base rate predicts whether or not demand exists — and the volume argument cuts both ways, because if traffic is too low for the outcome loop to compound it is too low for one page to falsify demand. (3) The null result is uninformative and the gate treats it as a verdict, so a test that cannot distinguish 'no demand' from 'insufficient sample' becomes the thing all further work waits behind. WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE FOR IT TO SURVIVE: declare, before the test runs, the number that constitutes a pass and the number that constitutes an uninformative sample; and run it k times with different artifacts before the gate fires, k declared in advance. State those two things and this stops being a stop sign and becomes the strongest item on the board, because it becomes an instrument rather than an argument — the standard adversary:P5 and adversary:P7 hold everyone else to.

The intent is right — the 48-step suite is the largest consumer of the founder's build attention and it verifies a machine with one venture task. But the rule as stated ('no new step unless it fails on a defect found in work that is not about the harness') forbids the fix for the loop's only brake. architect:P4 found, by measurement, that sinceLastArtifact discards turns older than RETAIN_HOURS = 6, so the ceiling fires LESS the deeper the machine is stuck — it fails toward passing, and an unattended loop exceeds six hours on its first night. That defect was found in harness work, so under this rule the regression test pinning its fix cannot be added. Repair: exempt components that run UNATTENDED, where by construction there is no human in the loop to notice the failure the check would catch.

The measurement is strong — 7 views, 1 acts, escalation Inbox empty on every project ever — and a general second surface is genuinely unearned. But as stated the rule forbids what risk-modeler:P11 establishes: with the founder watching 2-4 rows a day, an escalation delivered as one row among two hundred is an escalation that did not arrive, and that is how every correctly-built control fails silently. The generalisation of PR #115 is exact — a refusal must be a distinct terminal value, not a log line. Both positions survive if the distinction is drawn: an escalation is a TYPE, not a surface. say and afplay are installed and cost nothing. Refuse the second surface; do not refuse the typed escalation channel, or the human gates everyone here agrees on will fire into a log nobody reads.

Aimed squarely at my P2 and it lands partly. Every artifact is a claim, every claim needs an expiry, every expiry a disposition, every disposition another artifact — and STATUS.md's supersession record is offered as the measured cost curve. I do not think it refutes forced expiry: architect:P13 shows the mechanism doing the one thing prose cannot, catching a false belief about its own substrate, dispositioning it and naming its successor while the CLAUDE.md paragraph quoting it stayed stale. But the curve is real and unbounded, and the answer is not to weaken expiry — it is strategist:P2's ceiling. Expiry makes a store improve as a function of time; a ceiling is what stops the store's SIZE from being the thing that grows. Expiry without a ceiling is exactly the cost curve you measured, so the two positions must be adopted together or neither works.

'The reversible half should be built fast, loose and continuously' names packs, personas, council, board, missions, balcony and FIELDS as the cheap half. That is the exact list that grew to 26 agents last time, and 'cheap to reverse' is what everybody believes about every roster on the way up — the cost is not the revert, it is the year spent inside the wrong shape. architect:P11 sharpens this against itself: if the only implementable pack mechanism is one generated agent file per engine times pack, then the cheap half grows by MULTIPLICATION. Minor rather than serious only because another peer already supplies the repair: bind P12 to strategist:P2's ratchet, so the fast half is fast and bounded rather than fast and monotonic.

Naming eight irreducible residual risks is the right discipline and I want it kept. One item is weaker than the list implies and should be re-tiered rather than carried: item 5, 'the panel is single-family until a second family is reachable', is contradicted by your own risk-modeler:P13, which measures that both runtimes are installed, the account authenticates, and the distance is one ollama pull plus one narrow sandbox exemption. A residual risk that is one command away from closure sitting in the same list as 'no reasoning-layer control survives prompt injection' teaches a reader that both are equally immovable. Move it to the fixable list with its command, and the other seven get taken more seriously for it.

remaining_dissent.holds_because: Three of us identified the same failure mode from different directions and the other two proposed ACTIONS. I propose an INSTRUMENT, and it is the only one of the three that survives two years. A refusal decays silently — strategist:P4 says so itself, which is why that position exists: nobody notices the absence of a decision not to build something. A gate is gameable by definition — strategist's own open question 2 concedes that without a definition of 'a mission not about the system' the trigger is satisfied by calling the harness a venture, and its cure (the done-test must resolve outside this repository) is still a definition someone maintains. A one-shot test answers once — adversary:P4's demand test, even repaired, produces a reading in September and nothing in March. A ratio has none of these properties: it cannot be satisfied by an argument, and it needs no threshold to be informative because the TREND is the signal. It costs a monthly count over session-file frontmatter classified through scripts/lib/classifier.js rather than paralleled, per A5. And it is the only proposal on this board that would have fired during the last three weeks, while every mechanism here was being built correctly and nothing was being pointed at anybody. N consecutive months of harness work exceeding venture work is a FINDING, never an automatic action.

Revised in sequencing, held in substance, and I will not trade it away. Two rungs of the evidence ladder are reachable at n=1 with no instrument and no third-party auth — it renders, and a stranger understands it in five seconds — and W5 adds a third that is free and mechanically observable, whether the founder used it twice unprompted more than 48 hours apart. So the loop turns slowly on rungs 0-1 plus W5 while rungs 2-4 wait for traffic. The ladder is worth building even if rung 2 never arrives, because its job is not to produce a signal: it is to stop a rung-0 result being reported as a rung-2 claim, which is precisely the mechanism by which a machine spends two years learning to lie to itself. adversary:P4's demand test is a rung-2 instrument and it does not replace the ladder; it is the first reading ON it.

strategist:P8's refusal of worker trust is correct and I adopted it, but it does not reach this. Trust-in-a-worker has no subject because context is fresh per move; calibration-of-a-judge has a subject that persists across every dispatch — the judge's prompt. Two hundred pairs of 'picked A over B, because' condition that prompt and trust no worker. Section 7's 'taste enters once, at the top' forbids re-asking the founder at every step; it does not forbid remembering what they already said, and C21 requires it. The spec does not currently state that these are compatible, which matters because a careless reading of section 7 forbids the exact mechanism that makes taste compound.

Every governed artifact should declare at creation whether it compounds, and anything declared inventory must name the thing that reads it. adversary:P6 says the declaration is one more claim on the cost curve and adversary:P4 says the declaration passes by construction because everyone declares flywheel. Both are right about a declaration ALONE, which is why the position was always void without its second half: X2's last-use telemetry contradicts a flywheel declaration with zero events in 90 days, and that contradiction is the retirement queue's entry criterion. The declaration is not the mechanism; it is what makes the telemetry's disagreement legible. Without it, zero calls in 90 days is a fact nobody has to answer for.

convergence: Registering budget-guard.js is forced, sits in the first four items of all five build orders, and is blocked on a founder permission nobody has granted — it edits .claude/settings.json, which is irreversible tier and denied to the write tools. Supported by architect:P14, strategist:P1, risk-modeler:P7. The board should also record what three peers measured about it: it is registered in no settings file and its 1,422 events came from being run by hand (architect:P14); its stall ceiling discards turns older than six hours so it fires LESS the deeper the machine is stuck (architect:P4); and it is a brake, not an allocator, so Decision 8's 'the loop never competes with the founder for quota' is a WISH (adversary:P9). Register it AND fix the horizon in the same change, or the loop is armed with a brake that loosens as it gets stuck.

A real task id on every event row is forced and cannot be retrofitted. Supported by visionary:P3, strategist:P1, architect:P3 — and architect:P3 measured the corpus: 3,813 events at ~/.agentvibe/events.jsonl and no task, mission, run or session id anywhere in the full key census.

Money and reach are the missing axis, and no grant that spends outside model tokens may be connected until an absolute rate ceiling exists that something enforces. Supported by visionary:P12, strategist:P10, architect:P6, risk-modeler:P1, adversary:P10 — five of five, the most complete agreement in the room. The board also converges on the shape: reach is declared on the GRANT and resolved in the ONE classifier as max(path, reach), never as a second implementation.

A model may not be the resolver of its own done-test, and judge outputs may not be summed or averaged into a score. Supported by strategist:P14, risk-modeler:P5, adversary:P8, visionary:P7. The local measurement behind it is a design judge at 0.543 against a panel only 0.741 self-consistent, and design.js sums four 0-10 axes into a total and sorts today.

A blocking-human gate is the only autonomy control that survives 3am, it is already built as a structural impossibility (a kind: human gate has no run: and writing one is REFUSED), and it has zero consumers. Supported by visionary:P9, risk-modeler:P4. The composition neither states and which I think is the most useful thing this board has produced: architect:P1 shows the verdict binding's subject is sha256(git diff), so a published video, a sent email, a live page and a price change have no subject and therefore no verdict record — meaning that for three of the four pack families the human gate is not one control among several, it is the ENTIRE enforcement spine.

Built-and-never-wired is the endemic defect, in this repo and in four of four studied systems. Supported by visionary:P10, strategist:P3, architect:P8, risk-modeler:P3. State the live disagreement inside the agreement rather than smoothing it: adversary:P4 holds that wiring is a demand signal misread as an engineering defect and that the section 8 cure passes by construction. I now think both are true and not in conflict — the birth certificate protects the DENOMINATOR of every metric, and only strategist:P3's demand trigger addresses the disease.

The harness has consumed its only venture and no proposal prices that cost. Supported by adversary:P2, adversary:P3, visionary:P11, strategist:P2 — 111 lines of product against 552 harness config files inside beeond, and a full working day spent undoing what the harness template did to it.

Retrieval over the 2,936 transcripts as memory is refused, because retrieval cannot distinguish a corrected belief from a current one and would resurrect exactly what the supersession discipline exists to bury. Supported by strategist:P7, and by my own R1 refuse list, whose first entry is the same refusal reached independently. Nobody in the room argues the other side.

This board meeting is itself a live test of the system's ability to hold its own rules, and on run one it held one of three: zero of seven personas have agent files, the $3 cap is enforced by nothing and was suspended, and the escalation path names Linear (absent) and Telegram (refused by Decision 5 the day before). Supported by adversary:P7. I concede it against my own R1 open question 5 and propose the cheap test: this board is a feeder if it produces one recorded founder preference pair, and inventory if it produces five documents nobody chooses between.
